claims.text: Group IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloy powders are highly susceptible to oxygen uptake during processing.
Using TiH2 or ZrH2 precursors facilitates powder processing.
The process requires a two-stage thermal history consisting of vacuum hydride decomposition followed by high-pressure hot extrusion.
Hydride decomposition at 400-600°C under vacuum below 10^-5 Pa can produce metal powder without oxygen ingress or premature oxidation.
Extrusion at 1000-1200°C under ultra-high-purity argon or vacuum and pressure above 500 MPa ensures densification without cracking.
High-pressure hot extrusion suppresses nucleation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
The adapted process maintains a metastable single-phase BCC solid solution.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a single-phase solid solution.
Rapid hydrogen removal prevents segregation into brittle alpha-HCP phases.
Vacuum decomposition releases hydrogen without introducing oxygen.
Avoiding oxygen during hydride decomposition prevents brittle oxides and alpha-HCP phases that would raise the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
High hydrostatic pressure suppresses void formation during extrusion.
High hydrostatic pressure promotes solid-state diffusion and thereby helps maintain the metastable BCC phase.
BCC refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit weak temperature dependence of yield strength and retain more than 400 MPa yield strength at 1600°C.
Cast BCC refractory high-entropy alloys typically develop dendritic structures with severe compositional segregation.
Conventional vacuum arc melting or casting of Group IV-containing refractory HEAs typically causes severe oxygen uptake, alpha-HCP precipitation, and catastrophic cracking.
The proposed process will produce a dense, crack-free bulk alloy.
The proposed bulk alloy will have a homogeneous, single-phase BCC microstructure.
The proposed Group IV-containing alloy will exhibit yield strength above 400 MPa at 1600°C.
The proposed alloy will have significantly improved ductility relative to cast or oxygen-contaminated counterparts.

contradictions.description: The structural_mediator wording says the metastable BCC solid solution is 'suppressed by' rapid hydrogen removal and hydrostatic pressure, whereas the hypothesis and mechanism say those operations maintain or stabilize the BCC phase. This appears to be a wording-level reversal of the intended effect.
